messages.content: Durham changed again. Thursday's first meeting is now 8:15 a.m. at the South Regional Library branch southeast of downtown, not at the downtown office. I have not ticketed yet. Can you narrow the hotel choice before I send finance the final request? I care most about not creating a crazy early rideshare, staying near the $195/night reimbursable target, and having a straightforward breakfast.

I re-ranked the shortlist around that branch location. Rates still need a live check, but this is the practical comparison:

| Hotel | Est. 2-night total | Thu. early ride to branch | Breakfast / room setup | Cancellation | Read |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| SpringHill Suites Durham City View | about $420-$430 with tax | 13-18 min if leaving 7:15-7:25 | breakfast included; coffee maker and mini-fridge listed | likely May 12 by 11:59 p.m. | Best balance; still under target |
| Holiday Inn Express RTP/Southpoint area | about $465-$485 with tax | 8-11 min | breakfast included; coffee/fridge listed | often later, around May 13 by 6 p.m. | Shorter first ride, but borderline over cap |
| Lower-rate downtown option | about $385-$400 with tax | 15-20 min | breakfast extra or unclear; fridge not clear | earlier/stricter | Cheaper, but not simpler |
So the cheaper downtown option is not worth it even though it is roughly $30 less per night?

I would not take it for this agenda. The early ride is not materially better than SpringHill, and the savings get eaten by buying breakfast, dealing with uncertain in-room basics, and accepting a worse cancellation window. It is cheaper on paper, but less useful for an 8:15 start.
How much more is the closer chain once tax is in? I do not want finance to kick it back.

Compared with SpringHill, the closer chain is roughly $45-$60 more total after tax. More importantly, the pre-tax nightly rate I saw is around the top of the cap, possibly a few dollars over depending on the refundable rate. If finance treats $195 as strict, SpringHill is much safer.
If I leave SpringHill around 7:20, is that enough margin for an 8:15 start?

Yes. I would schedule the rideshare for 7:15 or 7:20. Even with a 25-minute ride, you are at the branch around 7:45. If the forecast looks rainy or there is a school-traffic alert, move pickup to 7:05.
Can you confirm the practical stuff on SpringHill again: breakfast, coffee maker, mini-fridge?

The current listing shows breakfast included, plus an in-room coffee/tea maker and mini-fridge for the suite category. I would still put a note on the reservation asking the hotel to confirm the mini-fridge and coffee maker, but it is a better match than the cheaper downtown room.
Okay. What exactly should I hold?

Hold SpringHill Suites Durham City View for Wed. May 14-Fri. May 16 on the refundable rate, ideally the one-bed suite if selectable, at about $184/night before tax. It keeps the hotel under the reimbursable target, preserves the easy breakfast plan, and the branch commute is manageable. Put May 12 on the calendar as the cancellation check. The RTP/Southpoint chain is only the backup if the branch agenda expands farther south.

messages.content: Quick Durham airfare check. SpringHill and the Wednesday outbound are booked. Friday now has a noon lunch with the library director, so show returns after 2 p.m. only. Avoid a rushed RDU transfer or a late ORD arrival.

| Return | Timing | Fare | Read |
|---|---|---:|---|
| United nonstop | 3:55p RDU-5:15p ORD | +$70 | Cleanest |
| AA via CLT | 2:25p-7:20p | base | Tight after lunch, connection risk |
| Delta via ATL | 4:05p-8:35p | +$15 | Not rushed, long day |

Pay for the nonstop if the fare is still live.
So the $70 is defensible?

Yes. It buys margin if lunch runs to 1, avoids a connection, and still gets you home before dinner. Book the 3:55-ish nonstop; if it disappears, take the 4:05 connection over the 2:25 unless lunch is shortened.

messages.content: Switching gears to Denver. I have a sector conference June 9-11: Monday evening reception at the conference hotel, Tuesday downtown sessions, and an optional Wednesday roundtable that ends at 10:45. Can you scan ORD-DEN flights and two or three hotels? United is fine if close, but I mostly need a Wednesday afternoon return and a hotel that does not blow the budget.
Sure. What hotel cap should I use, and should I assume economy with no checked bag? Also, do you already have the conference hotel block rate?

Economy, no checked bag. Hotel cap is $230 before tax. The block is $229 at the Sheraton Denver Downtown. Use it if the convenience is actually worth it, but please check whether the room has a refrigerator. A nearby place with breakfast could be better.

Flight scan from ORD, assuming you want enough time for the Monday reception and the Wednesday roundtable:

| Airline | Outbound Mon. Jun 9 | Return Wed. Jun 11 | Est. fare | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| United nonstop | 9:55a-11:40a | 2:15p-5:45p | about $286 | Best timing; no rush after 10:45 |
| American nonstop | 8:20a-10:05a | 12:35p-4:05p | about $248 | Cheaper, but return is tight |
| Southwest via MDW | 10:30a-12:10p | 1:50p-5:15p | about $262 | Works, but airport switch to Midway |
The United timing looks easiest. Is there a cheaper flight that still works after the roundtable?

Only modestly. The American return saves around $38 but would mean leaving the roundtable immediately and hoping security is light. Southwest is about $20-$25 less but shifts you to Midway. I would use the United nonstop as the working flight unless the fare jumps.
Okay, compare the hotels with that flight baked into the total.

Using the United fare and about $60-$75 for local airport/downtown transport:

| Hotel | Hotel total, 2 nights | Trip total estimate | Conference convenience | Breakfast / room basics | Dinner access | Read |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Sheraton Denver Downtown block | about $531 with tax | about $880-$895 | Best; reception and sessions in-house | breakfast not included; coffee maker; refrigerator appears request-only | on-site restaurants | Most convenient, but highest effective cost |
| Hampton Inn & Suites Denver Downtown-Convention Center | about $455-$465 with tax | about $805-$825 | 6-8 min walk | breakfast included; coffee maker and mini-fridge listed | many nearby restaurants | Best value if walking is fine |
| Hyatt Place Denver Downtown | about $495-$505 with tax | about $845-$865 | 5-7 min walk | breakfast/rate should be verified; mini-fridge listed | on-site bar plus nearby options | Middle option, but less clear value |
The Sheraton refrigerator being request-only makes me nervous. Is that enough to rule it out?

Not by itself, but it weakens the case for paying the block rate. If the Sheraton cannot guarantee a refrigerator and breakfast is extra, the convenience premium is closer to $80-$100 once breakfast is considered. I would call the block desk before relying on that room setup.
For the Monday reception, is staying at Hampton too annoying? I may not want to walk back late.

It should be manageable. The walk is short in normal weather, and a late rideshare back would likely be a small fare. Even two or three short rides would not erase the Hampton savings, and Tuesday sessions are still easy from there.
Can you give me the finance version in one compact table?

| Piece | Recommendation | Estimate | Why |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Flights | United nonstop ORD-DEN Mon. 9:55a-11:40a; return Wed. 2:15p-5:45p | about $286 | Clean timing after the 10:45 roundtable |
| Hotel | Hampton Inn & Suites Denver Downtown-Convention Center, 2 nights | about $455-$465 with tax | Under cap; breakfast included; coffee maker and mini-fridge listed; short walk to conference hotel |
| Local transport | Airport transfer plus one possible late rideshare after reception | about $60-$75 | No rental car needed |
| Estimated total | Flight + hotel + local transport | about $805-$825 | Lower than the Sheraton plan while keeping the conference convenient |

Recommendation: book the Hampton on a refundable rate. Keep the Sheraton as backup only if it can guarantee the refrigerator or drops to within about $40 total of Hampton after breakfast is considered.
